variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the HR12DE
variants.intro: The HR12DE is the naturally aspirated 1.2-litre three-cylinder petrol engine in Nissan's HR family . The engine code appears on the engine block itself, near the cylinder head or front timing cover, and on the VIN plate / V5C logbook. Similar codes commonly confused with the HR12DE: - HR12DDR - the turbocharged 1.2-litre DIG-T variant, fitted to the Juke 1.2 DIG-T and Note 1.2 DIG-S. Higher output (98 hp vs 80 hp) - see our HR12DDR engine page - HR16DE - the 1.6-litre four-cylinder HR engine, used in larger Nissan models - HR10DDT - the 1.0-litre turbo three-cylinder fitted to newer Micra and Juke models Why fitting the correct revision matters: The HR12DE shares the same block architecture as the HR12DDR but has different internals (pistons, connecting rods, turbo plumbing) - a turbo variant engine will not run correctly in an NA application and vice versa. Always confirm the exact code and any suffix letters before ordering.

items.question: What are the common problems with the Nissan HR12DE engine?
items.answer: The most common HR12DE issues are ignition coil failure (causing misfires and power loss from 35,000-60,000 miles) and auxiliary drive belt tensioner wear (screeching on cold starts from 5-8 years). Oil consumption can develop on higher-mileage examples (100,000+ miles) due to piston ring wear. → Read our full HR12DE failure guide
bullets: Coil failure: straightforward fix, £50-£150 per coil
Belt tensioner: belt and tensioner replacement required
Oil consumption: monitor oil levels between services

items.question: Which Nissan models use the HR12DE engine?
items.answer: The HR12DE was fitted to Nissan Micra IV (2010-2016), Note II (2012-2020) and Juke F15 (2012-2019) in the UK. It was also used in the Note e-Power hybrid as the petrol generator engine. → Check your exact model fitment
bullets: Micra: 1.2, 1.2 LPG
Note: 1.2, 1.2 e-Power
Juke: 1.2 (NA - not the DIG-T)

items.question: What's the difference between the HR12DE and HR12DDR?
items.answer: The HR12DE is naturally aspirated (80 hp, 106 Nm), while the HR12DDR is turbocharged (98 hp, 142 Nm). They share the same block architecture but have different pistons, connecting rods, and fuel systems - they are not interchangeable. → See our HR12DDR engine page
bullets: HR12DE: NA, 80 hp, fitted to Micra/Note/Juke 1.2 (non-turbo)
HR12DDR: Turbo, 98 hp, fitted to Juke 1.2 DIG-T and Note DIG-S

items.question: Is the Nissan HR12DE a reliable engine?
items.answer: Generally yes - the HR12DE is considered durable when properly maintained. Early 2010-2013 units may show more ignition coil issues, but the engine's core design is robust. Vibration is well-controlled thanks to Nissan's outer balancer design. Regular oil changes and spark plug service at 60,000 miles (100,000 km) are essential for longevity. → Get maintenance advice for your HR12DE
bullets: Good maintenance = 150,000+ miles achievable
Watch for: coil failure (35-60k), belt tensioner wear (5-8 years)
Proven reliable in taxi and fleet use
